game_concept: A strategy race set in Coastal Port – Cliffside Fort, a fort on the sea cliffs: the fisher must handle rogue waves while practicing conditionals (if / elif / else). Core idea – Nested Maze: Pick routes through nested if statements that branch inside branches.
theme: Coastal Port – Cliffside Fort: a fort on the sea cliffs
core_gameplay_loop: Construct a solution, execute it, inspect actual state and outputs, then revise until all mission goals pass.
secondary_mechanics: Hint tokens that reveal one line of code
player_objective: Debug ordering: Repair the reversed arithmetic instructions in the starter. add 15, then double. Match all 3 streams; preserve their order. Dataset 6, operand 15.
controls: Edit both node programs. IN reads the upstream queue; OUT sends to the next node. Step advances one cycle; Run checks every stream.
win_condition: The executed solution satisfies every output and world-state check.
lose_condition: The available unsuccessful execution checks are exhausted.
assets_style: Shared Kenney CC0 tile and audio assets with deterministic Canvas layouts; assets are not duplicated per game.
duplicate_check_notes: Unique combination of primary mechanic 'Nested Maze' (Week 3 slot 6), mission type 'Rival Race', and setting 'Cliffside Fort'. No other file shares this combination; games sharing the mechanic differ in mission/win condition and setting, and games sharing the setting use a different mechanic.

region.name: Coastal Port
region.mood: sea-shanty accordion with wave and gull ambience

tutorial: Read the objective, fixtures and command reference.
Build the circuit or route, or edit the node/adventure program.
Use Step to inspect state; Run checks the real outputs and goals.
Revise errors before using the remaining execution checks.
source_player_objective: Beat a rival AI to the sea wall by solving code steps involving route_score that move the fisher forward.
source_win_condition: Player progress reaches 100% before the rival does (rival speed 0.85).
source_lose_condition: The rival reaches the sea wall first, or lives reach 0.
hint: Follow the input through each operation. Compare every output, including negative inputs.
